passages.original: Hic locus manifeste refertur ad Judam : constat enim, usque ad Nativitatem Christi non defecisse principes 10 ex genere Judae, nec duces de femo- ribus ejus, usque ad Herodem regem, qui secundum fidem historiae, quam Josephus c scribit, alienigena fuisse, et per ambitionem in regnum Judaeorum di- citur irrepsisse. Statim ergo ut hoc factum est, et ut defecit dux de femoribus Judae, advenit ille cui re- gnum repositum, in quo, quomodo Gentes sperent, Evangelii fides et Ecclesiarum docet propagatio. Re- posita autem dicuntur ea quae opportuno tempore proferenda sunt, sicut et Christus in fine saeculorum advenisse dicitur, cum dicit Apostolus, Ecce nunc tempus acceptum (2. Cor. 6.), scilicet ad salutem Gentibus conferendam. Si vero quis in omnibus cu- piat cursum utriusque expositionis aptare, poest extorquere fortassis, ut etiam de Christo haec hoc modo videantur intelligi : Quia non deficiet Princeps ex Juda, id est, bi qui post resurrectionem ejus, Ec- clesiarum principes ordinantur : Et dux de femoribus ejus, duces quoque populi Christianorum, de femo- ribus Christi.
passages.english: This passage plainly refers to Judah. For it is agreed that rulers from the stock of Judah did not fail until the Nativity of Christ, nor leaders from his thighs, down to King Herod, who, on the trustworthy account of the history that Josephus writes, was a foreigner and is said to have crept into the kingdom of the Jews through ambition. So immediately when this happened, and when the leader from the thighs of Judah failed, there came the one for whom the kingdom was reserved, in whom the faith of the Gospel and the spread of the Churches teach how the Gentiles hope. Now things are said to be "reserved" which are to be brought forth at the fitting time, just as Christ too is said to have come at the end of the ages, when the Apostle says, "Behold, now is the acceptable time" (2 Cor. 6), that is, for bestowing salvation on the Gentiles. But if anyone wishes to fit the course of both interpretations in every point, he can perhaps wring [from it] that these words too may be seen to be understood of Christ in this way: "For a ruler shall not fail from Judah," that is, those who after his resurrection are ordained rulers of the Churches; "and a leader from his thighs," that is, the leaders too of the Christian people, from the thighs of Christ.
